sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Wayne County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Tax Commissioner sends and collects the bill, and the Wayne County Board of Tax Assessors sets the value. The commissioner's office is at 341 E Walnut St, Jesup, GA 31546, with a mailing address of PO Box 287, Jesup, GA 31598, and a phone line at (912) 427-5910. Office hours are 8:30am to 5:00pm.

One bill covers several governments. According to the commissioner's site, the office collects for the State, the City of Odum, the City of Screven, the county and the school board. Bills go to the owner of record on January 1 of the tax year, using values from the Chief Appraiser and Board of Assessors and millage rates adopted by each of those bodies.

For a question about value, call the assessor at (912) 427-5920. For a question about billing, payment or penalties, call the commissioner. The commissioner also acts as the state's tag agent, so the same counter handles vehicle registration.

sections.h2: What is Wayne County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Wayne County covers 641.81 square miles of land and had a July 2025 population estimate of 32,481. That is up 7.8% from the April 2020 base of 30,141. County offices sit in Jesup, and the county also contains Odum and Screven.

The county's own site points to the Altamaha River, which forms the northeast boundary with more than 60 miles of river frontage, and to Lake Lindsay Grace, about 4.5 miles south of Highway 84 on Highway 203. The lake covers roughly 240 acres of surface water.

  • Population density: 47.0 people per square mile in 2020.
  • Housing units: 13,180, with a 67.3% owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $162,800.
  • Median gross rent: $846, and 102 building permits were issued in 2025.
  • Residents 65 and older: 17.7%, with a mean commute of 28.0 minutes.

The Census Bureau also counts 11,061 households for 2020 to 2024 and says 85.8% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Median household income was $53,427, and 84.3% of households had a broadband subscription.

sections.h2: When are Wayne County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property taxes are normally due November 15, and bills are normally mailed by September 15. Mobile homes follow a separate cycle, with payment due April 1 and a 10% penalty when it is missed. Vehicle taxes follow the owner's birthday.

A mobile home owner who wants to declare a different value must file a return with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and March 15. The commissioner's pages add that unpaid property can be levied upon and ultimately sold, so the bill is worth settling before a listing goes live. Payment can be made at the Walnut Street office or through the county's online payment site.

After the due date, state law starts interest the next day at a rate that resets every January (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40). Then, 120 days after the due date, a four-step penalty begins at 5% and climbs to a 20% maximum under O.C.G.A. 48-2-44. Each step arrives 120 days after the last, so an old balance grows slowly at first and then reaches the ceiling.

Ask the commissioner for the exact payoff on the day you plan to close, since interest keeps running. If the taxes go unpaid long enough, the county may levy on the property and sell it, which is a path every seller wants to avoid.

sections.h2: What is the Wayne County assessment and appeal process?
sections.html:
You can appeal a changed value within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The notice shows the current value, the previous value, the reason for any change and estimated taxes at the estimated rollback millage. Complaints about the amount of tax are not grounds, because the appeal is about value.

File the appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors, PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. The board reviews its value again and tells you its decision. If you stay unhappy, the file goes to the county Board of Equalization for a hearing, and a later appeal can go to Superior Court. Arbitration is available as an alternative to the Board of Equalization, and the assessor's office can explain it.

Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value, and a taxpayer may file a return between January 1 and April 1 to state a different value. A return made during that window can start the appeal process if the board does not accept the declared figure. Real property returns renew automatically at the prior year's value until something changes.

sections.h2: Does Wayne County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, and Wayne County has local exemptions that replace the state amount when the local amount is higher. The exemption comes off the assessed value, which is 40% of fair market value. You must own and live in the home on January 1, and the application is filed with the Tax Assessor.

The commissioner's FAQ gives April 1 as the filing cutoff, while the property page gives March 1. Ask the assessor which date applies before you count on the exemption for the year. A late application starts with the next tax year, and once approved the exemption renews on its own until you move or change ownership.

Standing timber is a separate item. The commissioner says it is not taxed until it is sold or harvested, and then it is taxed on 100 percent of fair market value at the millage rate.

sections.h2: How should a Wayne County seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Treat the tax bill as a closing item and get a written balance first. Because the bill goes to the January 1 owner, a house sold in October or November can still produce a bill in the seller's name for the full year. The closing attorney divides it between the parties, and the commissioner's payoff figure shows what the title company must send.

  • Ask for balances on every open year, including penalty and interest.
  • Check whether the house sits in Odum or Screven, which adds a city bill.
  • Confirm homestead status so the buyer knows whether to apply.
  • Request a copy of your deed from the Clerk of Superior Court if the title company asks for it.
  • Ask whether a mobile home on the lot is billed separately, since those taxes are due April 1.

If a house has years of unpaid tax, start with the commissioner's payoff, then plan for the sale around that number.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Wayne County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: It is (912) 427-5910. The office is at 341 E Walnut St in Jesup and is open 8:30am to 5:00pm. Questions about value go to the assessor at (912) 427-5920.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: They are normally due November 15 each year. Bills are normally mailed by September 15. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal a Wayne County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, PO Box 174, Jesup, GA 31598. The appeal must challenge the value, not the size of the bill.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Wayne County taxes?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date, and a penalty of 5% is added 120 days later. It rises in steps to a maximum of 20% under O.C.G.A. 48-2-44. The interest rate resets each January.

faqs.q: What is the assessment ratio in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Assessed value is 40% of fair market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that figure, and the millage rate is applied to what remains.
